text:
julia: FYI — customer (mobile app) seeing SSE stream cut off mid-response, partial tokens delivered, client reconnect doesn't resume (they get a fresh response which duplicates work). Happening across Android carrier and some WiFi. Repro steps and logs below, asking infra + mobile-eng for triage.

devon: thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and any request-id from their calls? also sdk version?

julia: from customer: 
- SDK: mobile-js 1.4.2 (fetch-based streaming)
- Model: rwd-infer-8k (streaming chat)
- Repro: start stream -> after ~85-95s network toggles (airplane mode on/off, or moves from LTE->WiFi) -> stream closes with partial text, reconnect attempts show 401 sometimes or just new stream.
- Client log snippet: 
```
[10:12:03] STREAM_START id=req_9a3f...\n[10:13:28] GOT_CHUNK id=req_9a3f... chunk="Good morni"\n[10:13:29] NETWORK_CHANGE: event=wifi->cell\n[10:13:30] STREAM_ERROR id=req_9a3f... err="FetchError: network request failed"\n[10:13:31] RETRYING id=req_9a3f...\n[10:13:31] NEW_STREAM id=req_b7c2... status=200\n```
They also pasted the raw partial SSE payload (truncated):
```
event: message
data: {"delta":"Good morni"}

: keepalive
```
They said sometimes they see a server 401 on reconnect (token refresh race) and sometimes the reconnect returns a brand-new completion.

ops-bot: server logs for request req_9a3f... (ingress LB -> runtime): 
```
[ingress][3115550001] client_addr=10.12.34.56 request_id=req_9a3f... model=rwd-infer-8k route=/v1/stream status=499 msg="client closed before finish" duration_ms=90230
[runtime][3115550001] stream_writer: connection lost: write tcp 10.23.45.67:443->10.12.34.56:52344: write: connection reset by peer
[auth][3115550001] token: expires_in=22s at stream end=true
```

sandeep: quick read — two plausible failure modes here: (1) mid-stream token TTL expiry/race when the client flips networks and tries to reuse a stale token during reconnect, (2) network middleboxes/NAT or carrier-side timeouts dropping idle TCP state during the handoff. server logs show a 499 and a TCP RST (client reset) not an internal runtime exception. auth line shows token had ~22s left at end which is risky for reconnect workflows that assume long-lived tokens.

sandeep: immediate mitigations:
- mobile: ensure your client refreshes tokens proactively (start refresh at token_ttl * 0.3) or always fetch a fresh short-lived token before re-issuing a resumed stream.
- mobile: add an application-level keepalive comment event to the SSE path every 20s (e.g., `: keepalive\n\n`) or send a tiny empty event to keep carrier NAT state alive during dead periods. Many carriers drop mappings after ~90s idle.
- infra: consider bumping LB idle timeout for streaming routes to 3-5 minutes and ensure proxies forward TCP keepalive. also validate we don't aggressively close on slow clients.

devon: actionable asks for customer to help repro and for infra to investigate:
1) customer: capture a short tcpdump or Android bugreport showing the 4-way close / RST timing and attach (anonymize IPs).
2) customer: paste the HTTP request headers (mask Authorization) and the response headers if they saw a 401. we want `x-request-id`, `x-runtime-req` if present.
3) mobile-eng (devon): can we get the exact SDK code path they use for reconnect? are they trying to reuse the same SSE URL or re-auth?
4) infra (sandeep): check LB (ALB/Nginx) idle timeout, and whether we have any per-connection proxy buffer that could close on buffer full. Also check gateway `keepalive_timeout` and any TCP reset policy.

julia: customer provided x-request-id: x-req-77b5f3 and a snippet where reconnect returned 401 for one attempt and 200 for the next. I'll attach full headers to the ticket.

ops-bot: related recent deploy note: "stream-keepalive-patch" rolled 3 days ago to staging only. No change to prod LB timeouts.

sandeep: follow-up from infra triage: on prod we see LB idle timeout at 120s, conn-level TCP keepalive is enabled but carrier NAT on some mobile networks can still drop mapping ~90s when interface changes. we observed ~15% of mobile streams cross a network handoff window where client TCP state is invalidated. auth TTL of ~60s plus refresh race can cause a single failed reconnect (401) — client then issues a fresh stream which duplicates output.

sandeep: recommended longer-term fixes:
- server: emit periodic SSE comment pings from runtime for long-running responses (every 20s) so client-side middleboxes see activity.
- client SDK: auto-refresh tokens proactively and treat reconnect as a fresh request unless a resume token is returned by the service. (Note: current API doesn't support resuming partial completions; clients must re-issue with conversation history).
- product: consider adding a resume_token feature in the streaming wire protocol to allow safe continuation without duplicating work.

devon: for now ask customer to try a quick client workaround: enable SSE keepalive comments every 15-20s and refresh token at TTL*0.4. if they can reproduce with that we can close the loop. also send us the tcpdump + x-request-id.

julia: I've escalated to the customer success manager and opened a ticket with attachments. I'll paste the tcpdump and headers when they come in. thanks all :thumbsup:

devon: noted. marking P2 for now, will escalate to infra if we see more than 3 affected customers or a reproducible case in-house.

sandeep: leaving an infra action: "increase stream route idle timeout to 300s in canary" and add a short job to validate SSE comment ping is emitted.

julia: closing the chat for now, will update once customer confirms workaround.
